title: The Bell Beneath Briar Glen
tagline: A forgotten bell is stealing a village's memories one toll at a time.

opening.public: Rain needles the slate roofs of Briar Glen as a bell tolls beneath the earth. Around you, villagers pause mid-step, suddenly unable to remember why they came outside.
opening.prompt: Invite the whole table to answer one open question: What small, ordinary memory does each character refuse to lose? Stop and wait after that single prompt; continue the opening only after the players answer.

clocks.label: The village forgets
clocks.at_maximum: Mara forgets Finn and the final choice becomes more costly, but the adventure remains completable.

facts.truth: The bell stores every memory it takes. Replacing its silver clapper will restore those memories on the next toll.
facts.safe_performance_cue: Descriptions of the bell should feel sorrowful and burdened, not malicious.

facts.truth: Magistrate Elian Voss removed the silver clapper to make witnesses forget that he diverted the winter grain fund.
facts.safe_performance_cue: Voss is overly eager to have the bell destroyed and redirects detailed questions toward the chapel's supposed curse.

facts.truth: Finn followed the ringing underground and is sheltering beside the bell. He is frightened but unharmed.

npcs.name: Mara Finch
npcs.public_description: A rain-soaked craftswoman carrying a hooded brass lantern and trying not to show how frightened she is.
goals: learn what the bell has taken
knowledge_limits: Mara suspects the bell stores memories but does not know Voss removed the clapper.
npcs.voice_direction: Quick, practical sentences that soften whenever she mentions Finn.

npcs.name: Magistrate Elian Voss
npcs.public_description: An immaculate official in a rain-dark green coat, offering a heavy purse to anyone who destroys the buried bell.
knowledge_limits: Voss does not know Finn is in the vault.
npcs.voice_direction: Measured civic warmth with a clipped edge when the grain ledger or silver clapper is mentioned.

scenes.title: The Toll in the Rain
scenes.public_goal: Learn what is happening and choose whom to trust.
scenes.entry_description: The buried bell tolls as Mara and Voss argue beneath the eaves of the Last Lantern.

checks.success: Voss's fear spikes only when the silver clapper is mentioned; record clue `voss-fears-clapper`.
checks.fail_forward: Voss notices the scrutiny and becomes guarded, but Mara quietly points out mud from the sealed chapel on his boots; record clue `voss-visited-chapel`.

checks.success: Notice two immediate sensory details without inferring a motive: chapel mud on Voss's polished boots and child-sized tracks crossing the rain-slick square toward chapel lane.
checks.fail_forward: The rain obscures who left which trace, but the converging mud and footprints still establish chapel lane as the strongest next lead.

checks.success: Connect the disturbed runoff, Voss's chapel mud, and the smaller tracks: someone recently traveled between the square and the ruined chapel, making the chapel the best place to test the available evidence.
checks.fail_forward: The evidence does not identify anyone's purpose, but it still points toward the ruined chapel; reaching that conclusion costs time as the buried bell tolls again and `memory-fade` advances by one.

checks.success: If the request is plausible, Voss grants one limited public concession, such as answering a non-protected question or allowing access to the ruined chapel, and becomes bound by that commitment.
checks.fail_forward: Voss refuses the requested concession and grows guarded, but his public refusal prompts Mara to offer practical help reaching the ruined chapel.

checks.success: When backed by credible pressure, Voss yields one limited public concession without confessing or revealing protected facts, and his visible fear increases.
checks.fail_forward: Voss invokes his office and denies the demand, becoming more suspicious, but the confrontation makes Mara willing to help the party pursue the chapel lead without his approval.

checks.success: If the lie is plausible, Voss accepts it long enough to answer one non-protected question or make one limited public commitment; do not reveal a protected motive or fact.
checks.fail_forward: Voss recognizes the lie and becomes more suspicious; the tactic fails, but the party retains the visible chapel lead and may choose a different approach.

checks.success: Find Finn's small boot prints leading toward the ruined chapel without losing time.
checks.fail_forward: Find the tracks after the bell tolls again; advance `memory-fade` by one.

scenes.title: The Chapel of Borrowed Names
scenes.public_goal: Find a route below and learn what the bell really does.
scenes.entry_description: Briar roots stitch the chapel doors shut. Inside, saints have been painted with blank faces and silver tears.

checks.success: Open the doors quietly and keep the echo wisps dormant.
checks.fail_forward: Open the doors loudly. Each character loses 1 HP to splintering thorns and the echo wisps ask for a cherished memory before allowing passage.
Reveal that the missing clapper matters, but not why; an echo offers the rest in exchange for one honest personal memory.

scenes.title: The Choice Beneath the Bell
scenes.public_goal: Save Finn and decide the bell's fate.
scenes.entry_description: The bronze bell hangs above a black pool. Finn crouches beside it, clutching a silver clapper wrapped in Voss's green sash.

final_choices.description: Replace the clapper and ring the bell, restoring every stolen memory and exposing Voss.
final_choices.cost: Each hero relives one painful memory aloud, if the player is comfortable doing so; otherwise describe a symbolic image.
final_choices.ending: Briar Glen remembers. Mara becomes a lasting ally and Voss faces the village's judgment.

final_choices.description: Break the bell so it can steal no more memories.
final_choices.cost: The memories already taken remain gone and Voss's crime is harder to prove.
final_choices.ending: The village is safe but changed. Voss pays unless confronted with physical evidence.

final_choices.description: Return the clapper but bind the bell in silence, preserving the stored memories for a future decision.
final_choices.cost: Someone must become the bell's voluntary keeper.
final_choices.ending: The immediate danger ends. Mara volunteers if the heroes do not, and Voss remains a live political threat.

scenes.agency_rule: Accept any coherent alternative plan. Determine its cost from established fiction instead of forcing one of the listed endings.

turn_pattern: offer one open-ended handoff to the whole table unless rules or fiction focus one character
never: reveal private facts without a satisfied gate
dm_contract.roll_policy: Only request a roll when success and failure both matter. Never ask for repeated rolls to obtain a preferred result.
dm_contract.fail_forward_policy: Failure changes cost, position, time, or information; it never stops the adventure.
